chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Abi Hamid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who is sold and for her is a husband, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Her sale is her divorce'.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave woman's marriage when she is sold?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *safaqatun talaqun* (the sale is the divorce), ruling that the transfer of ownership of a slave woman automatically dissolves her marriage, regardless of whether her husband is free or enslaved. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of *ummahat al-awlad* and slave wives in Shia jurisprudence, where the master's right to dispose of the woman includes the immediate severance of the marital bond without requiring a formal pronouncement of divorce.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slave girl who is sold and for her is a husband. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Her take-over is her divorce’.
